brandTone: Industrial-credible. Specifications-forward. Quietly confident, not aggressive. We sell engineering, not anti-skater rhetoric. Avoid 'gotcha' framing — the buyer is a property manager or city planner solving a maintenance problem, not a skater-hater.
audience: Primary: facilities managers, transit-authority spec writers, school plant operations, condo board chairs, heritage conservation officers. Secondary: architects specifying built-in deterrents at design phase.

competitorReferences.preventer.ca: Closest Canadian competitor. Their tone is technical-clinical. We can be similar but slightly warmer. Their site is dated — opportunity for cleaner UX.
competitorReferences.www.skatestoppers.com: US incumbent — generic global. We win on Canadian climate specs and bilingual.
competitorReferences.www.maglin.com: Site furniture brand (benches/bins) — adjacent. Our deterrents fit on their hardware. Reference for tasteful industrial photography.
competitorReferences.classic-arch.com: Architectural product catalog. Reference for product detail pages with specs.

globalIdentity.colorMood: Industrial steel + safety-orange accent. Charcoal #1a1a1a primary, red #c8102e accent (Canadian-flag-coded), warm grey #7d8085 secondary. Avoid skater-aesthetic / graffiti / urban-grunge — wrong audience.
globalIdentity.typography: Sans-serif primary (Inter or similar). Geometric, slightly condensed for headlines. No display-serif. No script.
globalIdentity.imagery: Real product installs in Canadian context: TTC bus shelter, Vancouver waterfront, heritage Quebec stone. Macro shots of hardware. Worker-installation in-progress shots. NO skater-on-rail before/after composites — too aggressive.
antiPatterns: Aggressive headlines like 'Stop them dead' or 'Skater-proof'
Generic stock photography of generic urban scenes
doPatterns: Crisp product macros — stud, dome, edge strip
Workers installing on real Canadian hardscape
Climate context (winter snow on installed hardware)
Heritage approval signoff documents (faux but plausible)

heroStyle: Split layout: full-bleed product macro on right (e.g., stud installed on granite), value-prop headline + 4-step CTA path on left. NOT a giant urban hero scene with text overlay.
signatureElement: Animated grade-comparison slider on homepage — drag between '304 stainless (inland)' and '316 marine grade (coastal)' to see corrosion resistance after 10 years. Educational + memorable. Reinforces climate-aware positioning.

components.ProductCard: Macro hardware photo + product name + 1-line short + 'View specs' link. NO price (quote-only).
components.IndustryCard: Real-context photo (transit bus shelter, school courtyard) + industry name + use-case bullets count.
components.CityGrid: Map outline of Canada with 15 city pins + grid below. City detail card has population + transit authority + climate zone badge.
components.ClimateZoneBadge: Visual chip showing Zone 4 (warm coast) → Zone 7B (deep cold) with frost-depth annotation.
